Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Absolutely! Let me break down the main types of whiskey in simple terms:
Bourbon (American)
Made from at least 51% corn, which makes it naturally sweeter and smoother
Great for beginners because it's approachable and easy to sip
Think: caramel, vanilla, honey flavors
Price range: $23–$120+
Scotch (from Scotland)
Made from malted barley, often with a smokier, more complex taste
Can range from light and smooth to rich and peaty
Think: smoke, fruit, spice, sometimes earthy notes
Price range: $22–$500+
Rye (American)
Made from at least 51% rye grain, which gives it a spicier, bolder kick
More assertive flavor than bourbon
Think: pepper, spice, dried fruit
Price range: varies widely
Other spirits we carry include tequila, rum, vodka, and gin — each with their own unique profiles.

Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?

Seen • Just now
Good news — you don't need much! Here's what will help you get the most out of your bourbon:
The essentials (you probably already have these):
A glass — Any glass works to start, but a Glencairn glass or small wine glass is ideal because it lets you properly smell the aromas (a regular tumbler doesn't capture the aroma as well)
Water — Keep spring water or soft tap water handy. Adding a bit of water can "open up" the spirit and help you detect finer notes. Alternate sips of water and whiskey to clear your palate
Skip the ice if you're really tasting — ice dulls the flavors
Optional but helpful:
Unflavored, unsalted crackers or small slices of bread to cleanse your palate between sips
If you want a complete starter experience:

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Great question! Here's how to get the most out of your first bourbon experience:
Step 1: Pour
Pour about 3/4 of an ounce (a small amount) into your glass — you don't need much for tasting.
Step 2: Look & Smell
Hold the glass up to the light and notice the color. Then swirl it gently and take a few sniffs — don't stick your nose right in, just hover above the glass. You'll pick up caramel, vanilla, maybe some oak.
Step 3: First Sip (Neat)
Take a small sip and let it sit on your tongue for a moment before swallowing. It might feel strong at first — that's normal! Notice the sweetness and any spice on the finish.
Step 4: Add Water
After your first taste, add just a few drops of spring water or soft tap water. This "opens up" the spirit and helps you detect finer notes while taking the edge off the alcohol.
Step 5: Sip & Explore
Take your time between sips. Alternate with water to clear your palate. Notice how the flavors change as you go.
Pro tips:
Skip ice for your first tasting — it dulls the flavors
Have some plain crackers nearby to reset your palate
Don't rush — this is about discovering what you like!
Enjoy the journey! 🥃
